Package io.github.jspinak.brobot.startup.orchestration

Class FrameworkLifecycleManager

java.lang.Object
io.github.jspinak.brobot.startup.orchestration.FrameworkLifecycleManager
All Implemented Interfaces:
Lifecycle, Phased, SmartLifecycle
@Component public class FrameworkLifecycleManager extends Object implements SmartLifecycle
Manages the Brobot framework initialization lifecycle within Spring.

FrameworkLifecycleManager implements Spring's SmartLifecycle interface to ensure proper framework initialization after the Spring context is fully loaded. It orchestrates the critical startup sequence: loading images, preprocessing them for pattern matching, and initializing the state structure that forms the foundation of model-based GUI automation.

Initialization sequence:

  1. Spring context loads all beans and dependencies
  2. SmartLifecycle triggers this component (phase = MAX_VALUE)
  3. Image resources are loaded from the configured path
  4. Images are preprocessed for efficient pattern matching
  5. State structure is initialized with loaded resources

Key features:

  • Automatic startup via isAutoStartup() = true
  • Runs last in the startup sequence (phase = Integer.MAX_VALUE)
  • Graceful shutdown support through stop() methods
  • Status tracking via isRunning() for lifecycle management

Design rationale:

Using SmartLifecycle ensures that all Spring beans are fully initialized before the framework begins loading resources. This prevents dependency issues and ensures services like logging and configuration are available during startup. The late phase execution guarantees that custom beans can be registered before framework initialization begins.

In the model-based approach, proper initialization is crucial as it establishes the state model and preloads all visual assets needed for automation. This upfront loading improves runtime performance by avoiding dynamic resource loading during action execution.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start()
      Executes the framework initialization sequence after Spring context is ready.

      This method is called automatically by Spring when all beans are initialized. It performs the following critical startup tasks:

      1. Sets the image bundle path (default: "images")
      2. Preprocesses all images for pattern matching optimization
      3. Initializes the state structure with loaded resources
      4. Marks the component as running

      Side effects:

      • Loads all images from the specified path into memory
      • Creates image patterns and color profiles
      • Initializes the global state structure
      • Sets running flag to true

      The image path can be customized by modifying the imagePath variable or through external configuration in future versions.

      Specified by:
      start in interface Lifecycle

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops the framework lifecycle component.

      Called during Spring context shutdown. Currently performs minimal cleanup by setting the running flag to false. Future versions may add resource cleanup or state persistence logic here.

      Side effects: Sets running flag to false

      Specified by:
      stop in interface Lifecycle

    • isRunning

      public boolean isRunning()
      Checks if the framework startup component is currently running.

      Used by Spring to determine the component's lifecycle state. Returns true after successful initialization via start(), false after stop() or before initialization.

      Specified by:
      isRunning in interface Lifecycle
      Returns:
      true if the component has been started and not yet stopped

    • getPhase

      public int getPhase()
      Returns the startup phase for this lifecycle component.

      Returns Integer.MAX_VALUE to ensure this component starts last in the Spring lifecycle. This guarantees all other beans (services, repositories, configurations) are fully initialized before framework initialization begins.

      Lower phase values start first, higher values start last. Using MAX_VALUE ensures maximum compatibility with custom beans that may need to initialize before the framework.

      Specified by:
      getPhase in interface Phased
      Specified by:
      getPhase in interface SmartLifecycle
      Returns:
      Integer.MAX_VALUE to run after all other lifecycle components

    • isAutoStartup

      public boolean isAutoStartup()
      Indicates whether this component should start automatically.

      Returns true to enable automatic startup when the Spring context is initialized. This ensures the framework is ready for use without requiring manual intervention or explicit startup calls.

      Automatic startup is essential for the framework to function properly in Spring Boot applications where manual lifecycle management is not desired.

      Specified by:
      isAutoStartup in interface SmartLifecycle
      Returns:
      true to enable automatic startup with Spring context

    • stop

      public void stop(Runnable callback)
      Stops the component and executes the provided callback.

      This method supports asynchronous shutdown scenarios where Spring needs to be notified when shutdown is complete. Currently implements synchronous shutdown by calling stop() followed immediately by the callback.

      Future versions may implement asynchronous resource cleanup with proper callback notification after cleanup completion.

      Side effects:

      • Sets running flag to false via stop()
      • Executes the provided callback to signal completion
      Specified by:
      stop in interface SmartLifecycle
      Parameters:
      callback - Runnable to execute after stop completes, must not be null
